metadata.summary: CheXpert is a large chest radiograph dataset containing 224,316 chest radiographs of 65,240 patients. It includes automatically extracted labels for 14 observations from radiology reports, with explicit modeling of uncertainty in interpretation.
metadata.purpose: To serve as a standard benchmark for deep learning models in chest radiograph interpretation, particularly for handling uncertainty in radiology report-derived labels.

papers.title: CheXpert — A Large Chest Radiograph Dataset with Uncertainty Labels and Expert Comparison

ethics.privacy_measures: Data de-identified per HIPAA Safe Harbor standards.

extraction.notes: 基线卡仅来自 dataset_catalog.xlsx 真实元数据；其余字段需论文/README 或人工补充。
pending_verification: geography.countries 由局限文本启发式推断，待人工核实

known_limitations: Labels derived from radiology reports rather than direct image annotation, introducing report bias and linguistic ambiguity.
Single-center origin limits generalizability to other institutions, imaging protocols, or patient populations.
No demographic metadata provided; potential underrepresentation or bias unassessed.
bias_and_limitations.modifications: Yes — labels are algorithmically extracted and uncertainty-coded from radiology reports; no raw image modification reported.
bias_and_limitations.representativeness_concerns: 90%+ from a single US academic medical center; no information on geographic, ethnic, or socioeconomic diversity.
bias_and_limitations.missing_data: Demographic attributes (age, sex, race/ethnicity) are not included in the released dataset.

data_origin.selection_rationale: Radiographs were selected from the electronic health record (EHR) system at Stanford Hospital to represent common chest imaging encounters.

population.target_population: Patients who underwent chest radiography at Stanford Hospital.
population.missing_groups: Demographic subgroups (e.g., age, sex, ethnicity) are not reported in the source abstract; representativeness across populations is unknown.

annotation.annotation_method: Labels for 14 observations automatically detected from radiology reports using NLP; uncertainty labels (U, A, -, +) reflect report phrasing (uncertain, absent, negative, positive).
annotation.labeling_provenance: Labels derived from free-text radiology reports via rule-based and NLP methods; ground truth on validation/test sets established by board-certified radiologists.
annotation.label_noise_description: Report-derived labels contain inherent uncertainty and ambiguity (e.g., 'cannot rule out', 'questionable'), leading to imperfect ground truth.
